sections.title: Standards & institutions
sections.intro: Established standards, institutional guidance, and regulatory reference points. These documents are external to the Commons and have different purposes and legal standing.

items.title: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
items.note: A widely used risk-management reference for organizations developing or using AI; a useful point of comparison, not the Commons' framework.

items.title: NIST Generative AI Profile (AI 600-1)
items.note: Extends the AI RMF's risk considerations to generative AI, including characteristics of AI-enabled operating environments.

items.title: ISO/IEC 42001 — AI management systems
items.note: Requirements for an organizational AI management system; distinguishes management responsibilities from descriptive research questions.

items.title: OECD AI Principles
items.note: International reference principles on trustworthy AI, accountability, transparency, robustness and human-centered governance.

items.title: European Commission — AI Act overview
items.note: Official explanation of the EU AI Act, its obligations and application timeline. Consult the legal text for binding requirements.

items.title: Japan METI / MIC — AI Guidelines for Business v1.2
items.publisher: Japan METI & MIC · national AI governance guidance
items.note: Japan’s March 2026 AI business guidelines distinguish responsibilities across developers, providers and users. The official page includes English translations; these are non-binding guidance, not Commons standards.

items.title: OWASP GenAI LLM Top 10 (2026)
items.note: Current community-maintained application-security risks and mitigations for LLM systems; complements governance descriptions.

items.title: NIST Adversarial ML Taxonomy (2025)
items.note: A technical language for adversarial AI methods, attacker goals and mitigations; useful when distinguishing mechanism from speculation.

sections.title: Research & publications
sections.intro: Selected reports and original studies relevant to capability, reliance, cross-agent effects, assurance and incident reconstruction. Experimental findings retain their study-specific limits.

items.title: Stanford AI Index Report 2026
items.note: A broad evidence-oriented snapshot of AI development, adoption, technical performance and governance trends.

items.title: Task-Completion Time Horizons
items.note: Measurements of frontier agents' software-task time horizons; informative for capability and intervention-window questions, not a measure of all work.

items.title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
items.note: Analyzes failure patterns across multi-agent systems, including coordination, specification and verification limits.

items.title: Incident Analysis for AI Agents
items.note: A proposal for reconstructing agent incidents from system, context and activity evidence; a methodological comparator, not an adopted Commons framework.

items.title: Self-Propagating Misalignment in LLM Agents
items.note: Tests whether agent-written memory or files affect a successor; controlled setups and failed transfers matter to interpreting persistence.

items.title: After the Attacker Leaves: Carryover Attacks
items.note: Separates planting from later triggering via persistent state and scheduled tasks. Manual test wakes do not establish unattended deployment prevalence.

items.title: When Truth Is Distributed
items.publisher: Yan et al. · controlled multi-agent study
items.note: Examines how false testimony affects collective fact recovery and how a claim may spread after its original source exits.

sections.title: Commons papers & working references
sections.intro: Public materials produced by or maintained within this Commons. Exploratory and private research is deliberately excluded until separately reviewed for publication.

items.title: Founding discussion and glossary · publication of record
items.note: The preserved publication accompanying the 35 founding terms; its definitions and claim standings are a fixed, citable baseline.

items.title: Browse the 35 founding terms
items.note: Definitions, relationships and vocabulary/claim standings with navigation to relevant evidence.

items.title: Evidence Library
items.note: Attributed findings, source families, cases and relationships, with limitations and withdrawal notices preserved.

items.title: Evidence Library publication policy
items.note: Explains why publication status, source inspection and independent verification are different judgments.

items.title: Evidence coverage and open gaps
items.note: Shows where published findings have explicit term relationships—and where they do not, without implying that unlinked evidence is absent.

items.title: Question-based research paths
items.note: Editorial starting points that connect governance questions with selected records and their limitations; not an exhaustive literature review.

sections.title: Related initiatives
sections.intro: Independent collections and research organizations that offer different lenses on AI incidents, security, safety and governance. Inclusion does not mean methodological agreement.

items.title: AI Incident Database
items.note: Searchable reporting on AI harms and near harms. Incident records may depend on the same underlying reporting sources.

items.title: MIT AI Risk Repository
items.note: A cross-framework inventory of AI risks with causal and domain classifications; helpful for comparing terminology and coverage.

items.title: MITRE ATLAS
items.note: Documented AI-related adversary tactics and techniques drawn from observed attacks and realistic demonstrations.

items.title: OECD AI Incidents and Hazards Monitor
items.note: Tracks media-reported incidents and hazards using automated aggregation; review original reporting before treating entries as verified events.

items.title: UK AI Security Institute
items.note: Research and evaluations concerning the risks and capabilities of advanced AI systems, with separate institutional aims from the Commons.
